conflicts: Nd nuclear magnetic-moment ratio mu(143)/mu(145): 1.60861(2) from the mean A-ratio of the 4f4 6s2 5I levels (Childs & Goodman 1972) and 1.60883(4) from ENDOR (Halford 1962), versus 1.626(12) from atomic-beam resonance (Smith & Unsworth 1965); all as quoted in Persson arXiv:0904.0516 Table 2. Spalding 1963 gives 1.60860(36).
Nd isotopic abundances: NIST composition table gives 142Nd 27.152(40) % and 143Nd 12.174(26) %; the IAEA/ENSDF table gives 27.153(40) % and 12.173(26) % (last-digit difference only).

Lifetime of 20300.875 cm^-1 (J=5): Biemont 2004 measured 12.7(1.0) ns, but with the NIST A values of its lines (sum 9e+07 s^-1, Stockett 2011) tau x sum(A) = 1.14 > 1; the Den Hartog 2011 value 10.6 ns (second-hand, basis of the NIST A values; tau x sum(A) = 0.95) is kept as the entry and Biemont as alternative. Marek & Stahnke 1980 give 11.8(0.8) ns, Gorshkov 1982 11(1) ns

Lifetime of 21345.572 cm^-1 (J=6): Den Hartog 2011 value 21.8 ns (second-hand via Ryder thesis Table 5.2) is inconsistent with the NIST A value 6.7e7 s^-1 of the 494.62 nm line (1/A = 14.9 ns); the lifetime is therefore stored only under "alternatives" and not as the level lifetime. Original paper needed to resolve (possible level/J mix-up between 21345.572 J=6 and 21345.837 J=4 in one of the sources)
Lifetime of 23996.513 cm^-1 (J=6): 20.1 ns (Den Hartog 2011 via Ryder thesis) vs NIST A = 5.6e7 s^-1 for the 462.32 nm line (tau x A = 1.13)
not_found: radiative lifetimes: Den Hartog, Fittante, Lawler, J. Phys. B 44, 225001 (2011) (100 levels) itself is still closed (OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar list no open copy; IOPscience PDF returns a bot-check page; no arXiv/OSTI copy). 84 of its 100 lifetimes were recovered second-hand from the open thesis that adopts them (Ryder, Wayne State 2011, Table 5.2; the rows shared with Putnam, Windsor 2014, Table 6.1 agree), without uncertainties; the other levels are still missing. The drawn level 21345.572 has a second-hand value (21.8 ns) that fails the tau x A check and is kept only as an alternative. (Verification pass: the earlier statement that the drawn levels 21572.610 and 25518.7 were missing was wrong; Ryder Table 5.2 prints 11.3 ns and 9.3 ns for them and both are now entered.)

Marek & Stahnke, Z. Phys. A 298, 81 (1980) and Gorshkov et al. (1982) Nd I lifetimes: originals not opened (Springer paywall; Soviet journal not online); only the 4+3 values quoted in Biemont 2004 Table 2 and Ryder Table 5.2 are entered as alternatives

transition probabilities / branching fractions: Stockett, Wood, Den Hartog, Lawler, J. Phys. B 44, 235003 (2011) (236 lines) is paywalled; the NIST ASD A-values already on the site come from it. Second pass: still closed (OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar: no open copy). The laser-induced-breakdown gA values of the Ryder (2011) and Putnam (2014) theses were read but not entered (lower accuracy than the NIST/Stockett values already on the site)

hyperfine constants of the 4f4 6s2 5I5-5I8 levels and of 5I4 for 145Nd (Childs & Goodman, Phys. Rev. A 6, 1772 (1972)): paywalled; a web-search snippet gave A(145Nd, 5I4) = -121.627(27) Mc/s (Spalding 1963) but the page showing it could not be opened, so it is not entered. Second pass: OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar list no open copy; the open citing paper (Persson, Atoms 6, 63 (2018)) tabulates only the 7L/7K constants and the mean A-ratio, not the 5I constants
hyperfine constants of the odd-parity levels the site draws (4f4 6s6p 5K*, 5H*): none located
isotope shifts of Nd I lines (neutral atom): only Nd II (ion) isotope-shift work was found openly; none entered
precise (laser/frequency-comb) transition frequencies for Nd I: none located

laser-cooling lines: Nd has not been laser-cooled (Hovhannesyan & Lepers, arXiv:2209.15479, state it 'has not yet been considered for laser-cooling'); that paper is a level-energy modelling study and proposes no specific cooling line, so no 'use' annotation is given
notes: Nd I lifetimes (second pass): 15 levels measured by Biemont et al. 2004 (opened, Lund University repository) and 84 lifetimes of Den Hartog, Fittante, Lawler 2011 read second-hand in two open theses (Ryder 2011 Table 5.2; Putnam 2014 Table 6.1) (method "compilation", no uncertainty printed; the original abstract quotes +/-5%). Where both exist the directly opened Biemont value is the entry and the Den Hartog value sits under the level key "alternatives" (each alternative names its quantity), except for 20300.875 cm^-1 where the Biemont value fails the tau x sum(A) check (see conflicts). Lifetimes were checked against the NIST A values: tau x sum(A) <= 0.96 for all drawn levels except those listed under conflicts. The branching-fraction paper (Stockett 2011) and the ground-term hyperfine paper (Childs & Goodman 1972) remain closed. Hyperfine A constants are for the even-parity metastable levels 7L5, 7L11, 7K4 (second-hand) and the ground level 5I4 of 143Nd (abstract of the original paper). Nuclear spins 7/2 for 143Nd and 145Nd from the IAEA/ENSDF ground-state table (https://nds.iaea.org/relnsd/v1/data?fields=ground_states&nuclides=143nd).
